typed_values.description: Every setting declares one type from a closed vocabulary: text, integer, number, boolean, selection, secret, duration, url. A value that does not parse as its declared type is refused rather than coerced.
typed_values.claim_boundary: Typing is structural validation of caller-supplied text. No value is interpreted, executed, or applied to a live connector.

validation.description: A configuration is validated as a whole. An undeclared key is refused outright, a missing required setting is reported, and every failure is a diagnostic string that names the offending key.
validation.claim_boundary: Validation is local and deterministic. It does not prove that a connector accepts the configuration.

defaults.description: A declared default is itself validated against the declaring type when the schema is built, so a schema with an invalid default refuses every configuration instead of applying a bad default.
defaults.claim_boundary: A default is a value the host supplies, not a value the provider chose.

secret_refs.description: A secret setting carries an opaque handle of the form secretref:<vault>:<name>. A value that looks like a literal secret, by key prefix or by long unbroken token shape, is refused outright and never stored, returned, or logged. A secret setting may not declare a default.
secret_refs.claim_boundary: This contract never reads, resolves, or transmits the secret itself. Vault resolution and rotation remain DEFERRED-EXTERNAL.

dependencies.description: A setting may depend on another setting's value. A value supplied while its dependency is unmet is refused, and a dependency cycle or an undeclared dependency key makes the whole schema invalid.
dependencies.claim_boundary: Dependencies are declarative gating, not an execution order.

conditional_visibility.description: A setting may declare the values of another setting under which it is visible. A value supplied while the setting is hidden is refused rather than silently accepted.
conditional_visibility.claim_boundary: Visibility is a data predicate. This contract renders no UI.

migration.description: A configuration migrates from a declared previous version by rename, deterministically and with the applied renames reported. An unknown source version is refused, and a key the schema does not declare is carried through untouched and reported, never silently dropped.
migration.claim_boundary: Migration renames and carries values. It does not transform a value's semantics or contact a provider.

acceptance.secret_handling: opaque handles only; literal secrets refused outright; never stored, returned, or logged
acceptance.fail_closed: a structurally invalid schema refuses every configuration
acceptance.determinism: diagnostics and migrations are deterministic and ordered
